articles.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
articles.summary: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).

articles.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
articles.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

articles.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
articles.summary: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

articles.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
articles.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

articles.title: Helix Carbon says it can make iron cheaper by recycling blast furnace pollution
articles.summary: The steel industry is a big polluter, but Helix Carbon can upcycle pollution from blast furnaces to drive down emissions and improve margins.

articles.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
articles.summary: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."

articles.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

articles.title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device
articles.summary: Fusion power startup Cambridge Heavy Industries is building a small, laser-powered fusion device to fuel the coming wave of fusion power plants.

articles.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt
articles.summary: Fusion power plants will need a lot of lithium, and Licube is preparing to be a key supplier.

articles.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
articles.summary: The San Francisco startup aims to help battery and chip manufacturers identify defects on production lines, reducing downtime and costly mistakes.

articles.title: Rivian’s startup Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
articles.summary: Field also worked on Apple's secretive car project and oversaw development of the Tesla Model 3.

articles.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
articles.summary: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
articles.summary: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

articles.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
articles.summary: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality.

articles.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
articles.summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

articles.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
articles.summary: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

articles.title: MIT startup says it can turn diesel trucks into cheaper hydrogen haulers — see it at Disrupt
articles.summary: Diesel is expensive and polluting, and LNK Energies says it has come up with a way to replace it with hydrogen, all while undercutting diesel on cost.

articles.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
articles.summary: Google is making it easier to build and use personal Android apps created with AI, without having to make them available to everyone on the Play Store.

articles.title: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s
articles.summary: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
